decisions.decision: Add exactly two new files, internal/domain/invariant_model_test.go and internal/domain/source_guard_test.go, and leave internal/domain/core_test.go and internal/domain/id_test.go byte-identical. No production file under internal/domain changes.
decisions.rationale: Measured baseline: devbox run --pure -- go test -v -count=1 ./internal/domain reports 16 passing tests, and three of them (TestDeterministicControlSequenceNeverAllowsAfterStop, TestDeterministicRandomSequencePreservesPermitRevisionInvariant, TestStatefulDeterministicModelSequence) are already deterministic model-based sequences. The M1 gap is not that model-based testing is absent, it is that the existing sequences sample the space (100 revisions, 500 LCG draws, 64 seeds on one fixed happy-path script) instead of closing it, and that two of the five Safety Invariants named in docs/architecture/validation.md section 2 have no test at all. Re-implementing what passes would burn the remaining retry budget on work that produces no new evidence.

decisions.decision: Finitize the claim "stop effective後の副作用permitが全command sequenceで0" with a three-layer closure argument instead of a longer random walk: L1 decision closure, L2 effective-control closure, L3 effect-construction closure. Each layer is an exhaustive nested enumeration, and each asserts its own enumerated case count against a named constant declared in the test.
decisions.rationale: L1: Permit reads only (control.Mode, control.Found, control.Revision, control.Scope, request.Kind, request.ControlRevision, request.FencingToken, request.ExpectedFencingToken, request.Resource); Scope and Resource flow into the returned decision and never into an allow/deny branch (internal/domain/control.go lines 234-281). The allow/deny function is therefore total over ControlMode x PermitKind x revision-relation x fence-relation, a space of order 9 x 10 x 3 x 3, so enumerating that cross product decides Permit for every possible input rather than for a sample. L2: EffectiveControl is a pure fold that keeps at most one surviving intent per scope, so no state beyond that map is carried across a sequence; exhaustive BFS over every intent sequence up to length 4 drawn from a 21-symbol alphabet (3 scopes x 7 modes, strictly increasing revisions) covers every stop/resume/overlap ordering. L3: EffectFromPermit is the only Effect constructor, so counting constructed effects at every L2 prefix whose effective mode is a stop mode and asserting the counter is exactly 0 closes the claim at the only boundary where a side effect can become durable. Asserting the enumerated counts against constants is what stops a later refactor from silently shrinking the space while the test still reports PASS.

decisions.decision: Forbid math/rand and crypto/rand anywhere in package domain, including test files. Generate sequences by exhaustive nested enumeration where the space is closed, by an explicit table where the space is a designed matrix, and by the existing seeded LCG (next = next*1664525 + 1013904223) with the seed as the loop index where varied-but-reproducible values are still wanted.
decisions.rationale: docs/architecture/validation.md section 9 forbids promoting a test whose result varied on the same candidate. A test that draws no entropy from outside its own source cannot vary between runs on the same candidate, so the flaky policy is satisfied by construction rather than by process. Go's global math/rand has been auto-seeded from a random value since Go 1.20, so importing it would reintroduce exactly the run-to-run variance the policy prohibits; time.Now would reintroduce real-clock dependency, which roadmap M1 forbids.

decisions.decision: Prove "credential fieldがdomain schemaに存在しない" with a go/ast scan of the domain package's own source files that collects every struct field name and every json struct tag, normalizes them (lowercase, underscores removed) and matches them against a closed deny list, with positive and negative controls asserted in the same test.
decisions.rationale: The existing TestSchemasRejectSensitiveFieldNames covers only contracts/schemas and works by substring match on file text. That technique cannot be reused on the Go side: internal/domain/control.go legitimately declares PermitCredential PermitKind = "credential" as a permit-kind value, so a text grep for "credential" false-positives on correct code, while the bare substring "token" would false-positive on FencingToken, which appears in eight structs. Matching declared field names and json tags rather than file text distinguishes "the domain names a credential-shaped field" from "the domain names the act of requesting a credential". The deny list must be precise (password, passwd, credential, credentials, secret, apikey, privatekey, accesstoken, refreshtoken, bearer, sessioncookie, authorization, rawprompt, rawproviderout) and must exclude the bare word token, with the positive controls (Password, APIKey, RawPrompt, ClientSecret) and the negative controls (FencingToken, ContractDigest, PreviousFencingToken, PermitCredential as a const name) asserted so the matcher itself is verified rather than trusted.

decisions.decision: Keep the source-level guard inside internal/domain as internal/domain/source_guard_test.go rather than extending internal/contracts, and do not change ci/components.json.
decisions.rationale: internal/ci/planner.go computes a component evidence key as the sha256 of every tracked file matching the component roots, public contracts and contract dependencies, plus ci/components.json, go.mod, go.sum and devbox.lock. The domain component's roots are internal/domain/**, so a guard living there is automatically invalidated by any future domain change and is automatically executed by make component-domain. Putting it in internal/contracts would require adding internal/domain/** to that component's contract_dependencies, which is a cross-boundary manifest change, and would silently stop covering the guard if that edge were ever dropped. The cost is that this one test reads its own package directory from disk; that is a structural guard over tracked source, not a domain state test, so validation.md section 2's ban on filesystem use in domain state tests is respected as written.

decisions.decision: Prove "database／GitHub／Provider dependencyなし" mechanically with an import allowlist asserted from the AST, split between non-test and test files, and record devbox run --pure -- go list -deps ./internal/domain as an evidence check showing the transitive dependency set is stdlib only.
decisions.rationale: Measured today: non-test domain files import only errors, fmt, sort, strings and time, and go list -deps ./internal/domain resolves to stdlib plus the package itself with no third-party path. An allowlist asserted in the test converts that measurement into a standing gate; go list -deps recorded as an argv converts it into evidence a gate reader can re-run. The split is required because the guard test itself must import go/ast, go/parser, go/token, os, path/filepath and sort to read its own package, which non-test files must never do. The test additionally denies net, net/http, database/sql, os/exec, math/rand and crypto/rand everywhere in the package, and denies the selectors time.Now, time.Since and time.Until in non-test files, because a stdlib-only dependency set does not by itself exclude a real-clock read.

decisions.decision: Assert "expired tokenで状態が前進しない" as returned-value equality, not merely as a non-nil error: on every rejecting input the returned Execution, Lease or Requirement must be byte-equal to the input including its Version field.
decisions.rationale: Every rejecting path in internal/domain/lease.go returns the unmodified input (AcceptExecutionResult, StartExecution, MarkExecutionLost, RenewLease, ExpireLease all do), so the stronger property is true today and is the property the invariant actually names. Checking only errors.Is(...) would still pass if a future refactor bumped Version before validating, which is precisely a state that has moved forward under a stale token. The existing TestLeaseFenceAndExpiryRejectOldResults checks the error and discards the returned value.

decisions.decision: Prove "completed RequirementはStable Releaseを参照する" by exhaustive BFS to fixpoint over the DecideRequirement command closure (11 statuses x 9 command kinds) asserting RequirementCompleted is unreachable, then asserting that CompleteRequirementFromRelease is the only producer of that status and that it demands a valid StableReleaseProof and writes a non-zero StableSnapshot derived from that proof.
decisions.rationale: The invariant is a reachability property, and reachability over a finite labelled transition system is decidable by closure, so this is an exhaustive proof rather than a sample. It also pins the current architecture: DecideRequirement declares no completed command kind, and CompleteRequirementFromRelease (internal/domain/model.go lines 455-470) requires status == evaluating and proof.valid(). If either fact is ever weakened, the closure changes and the test fails, which is the intended resistance. Increment gets the same treatment (12 statuses x 12 command kinds) with the reached edge set compared against the transition table in docs/architecture/domain-model.md section 5, so a forbidden edge cannot appear silently.

decisions.decision: Prove "capability evidence欠損時にpromotableにならない" by exhaustive powerset enumeration over three capabilities: evidence present, Verified, Fresh and candidate-digest agreement per capability, crossed with RollbackEvidence and ResumeEvidence, asserting CanPromote and PromoteRelease succeed on exactly the fully present, verified, fresh, digest-matching, rollback-and-resume case and on no other.
decisions.rationale: The existing TestReleaseGateRequiresEveryFreshCapabilityAndRecoveryEvidence checks one missing-evidence case and one stopped-control case. The gate is a conjunction over per-capability flags, so the only way to claim every deficient combination is rejected is to enumerate the product; the space is of order 2^(3*4) x 2 x 2, which is small enough to enumerate outright. PromoteRelease must also be enumerated against every ControlMode so that a stop mode blocks promotion regardless of how complete the evidence is.

decisions.decision: Hold the whole internal/domain package within the 30-second edit-feedback budget, and require the implementer to measure and report the wall time of devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/domain.
decisions.rationale: docs/architecture/validation.md section 7 sets 30 seconds for the format/lint/domain gate, and internal/domain is not run by one target: make component-domain, component-control-plane, component-runner, component-reconciler and component-release all run go test ./internal/domain, so any cost is paid five times per full evidence sweep. The chosen bounds (length-4 sequences over a 21-symbol alphabet, roughly 2 x 10^6 pure function calls) are sized for well under a second; the budget is stated so that a later widening is a deliberate decision instead of an accident.

decisions.decision: Record the result as a single component evidence artifact .agents/v2/evidence/V2-010-domain.json with id ev-v2-010-domain, task_id V2-010, component domain, and evidence_key equal to the domain key reported by devbox run --pure -- make evidence-keys at the code commit; register it in .agents/v2/evidence/index.json with result passed and evidence_hash equal to the sha256 of the artifact bytes. Completion is defined as the index registration being green under internal/contracts, not as the domain test passing.
decisions.rationale: TestActiveEvidenceIndex enforces a bijection between .agents/v2/evidence/*.json and the index entries and recomputes evidence_hash as the sha256 of the artifact file, so an unregistered artifact and a stale hash both fail the ledger test; gate rule G2 in docs/operations/v2-task-dag.md reads exactly those fields. task_id is V2-010 because V2-010 is the producer: the precedent ev-v2-009-release-contract carries id of the verified deliverable and task_id V2-040 of the producing task, so attribution stays with whoever ran the checks. The domain evidence key depends only on internal/domain/**, ci/components.json, go.mod, go.sum and devbox.lock and not on .agents/**, so committing the artifact does not move the key and no aggregate re-issue is needed inside this task.

decisions.decision: Use a two-commit checkpoint (commit A: the two test files; commit B: the evidence artifact and its index entry), push one commit at a time after the parent commit's CI is green, and re-run devbox run --pure -- make check after commit B.
decisions.rationale: docs/architecture/validation.md section 11 and docs/operations/v2-task-dag.md section 10 both record the two measured constraints: gitleaks git scans committed history only, so a make check run before the evidence artifact is committed proves nothing about the 64-hex evidence_key inside it, and scripts/verify-parent-ci.sh requires a successful attestation on the parent commit, so two commits pushed back to back fail spuriously on the second one. The evidence_key must also be read at commit A, after the test files exist, or it will not match the key a gate reader recomputes.

decisions.decision: Do not modify any existing evidence artifact, any task-state file, the M0 aggregate attestations, ci/components.json, the Makefile or any production file. If an exhaustive enumeration finds a real Safety Invariant violation in production code, stop and escalate instead of fixing it.
decisions.rationale: A production fix is a different change with a different blast radius (internal/domain is a dependency of eight components) and would turn a verification task into an implementation task without a Work Order. The retry budget for V2-010 is two attempts with two remaining, and V2-010 is the successor of the already exhausted V2-007; spending an attempt on an unplanned production change is the failure mode that exhausted the predecessor. Existing evidence and task-state bytes are pinned by TestCanonicalTaskStateMigration and TestActiveEvidenceIndex, so editing them fails the ledger.

risks: Exhaustive enumeration can exceed the 30-second domain feedback budget of validation.md section 7, and internal/domain is executed by five component targets, so the cost is paid five times. Mitigation: bound the intent sequence closure at length 4 over a 21-symbol alphabet and report the measured wall time.

An import allowlist is deliberate resistance and will fail on a legitimate future import such as slices or maps. That is intended: widening the domain's dependency surface must be an explicit edit, not a silent one.

The source guard reads its own package directory. If the glob is written so that it can match zero files, the guard passes vacuously; the test must assert a minimum scanned-file count and fail on an empty set.

A deny list that includes the bare substring token would fail on FencingToken, and one that matches file text rather than declared field names would fail on the legitimate PermitCredential permit kind. The matcher must be name-based and must assert its own positive and negative controls.

Committing the evidence artifact changes .agents/**, which staleness the task-ledger component key and therefore the recorded M0 aggregate attestations. V2-010 must not regenerate them; whether M1 needs its own aggregate attestation is a gate-scope question for V2-011.

Enumerating a closed space can still miss an invariant if the property asserted inside the loop is weaker than the invariant. Every loop must assert an outcome (denied, unchanged value, unreachable status) and an enumerated case count, not merely absence of a panic.

M1 lists Priority Assessment among its deliverables, but internal/domain exposes PriorityAssessment as a data record with no comparison or starvation-prevention function, and validation.md section 2 lists priority comparison and retention eligibility as domain test subjects with no production counterpart. Verifying an absent behaviour is impossible, so V2-010 covers only the five named Safety Invariants; whether M1 gate V2-011 also requires a priority comparator and retention eligibility rules is a milestone-scope judgement that belongs to product_orchestrator, not to this Work Order.

V2-010 is the successor of the exhausted V2-007. If V2-010's complete transition omits V2-007 from input_refs and output_refs, V2-007 stays an unsettled failed task and gate rule G4 blocks V2-011 permanently. The transition is written by the coordinator, but the Work Order must carry the requirement so a resuming agent cannot lose it.
